Package com.csse3200.game.components

Class StatusEffectsControllerComponent

java.lang.Object
com.csse3200.game.components.Component
com.csse3200.game.components.StatusEffectsControllerComponent
public class StatusEffectsControllerComponent extends Component
Holds the status effects currently on an entity and drives them, treating every one of them as a plain StatusEffect so that nothing here depends on any concrete effect.

Effects are ticked once per frame in update() and dropped when they report done. The query methods (isConcealed(), getStatMultiplier(Stat), getTint()) combine the answers of the effects still running. They are pure reads: an effect past its deadline is ignored the instant it expires, but it is only taken off the list, and its removal callback only runs, on the next frame update. That keeps renderers and AI, which query every frame, from triggering lifecycle callbacks mid-query.

  • Method Details

    • isConcealed

      public static boolean isConcealed(Entity entity)
      Returns whether hostiles should currently be unable to find, chase or damage the entity. An entity without a controller is simply not concealed.

      This is the one question enemy AI, boss pursuit and contact damage ask. It names no ability, so any effect that reports StatusEffect.concealsOwner() hides whoever is wearing it.

      Parameters:
      entity - the entity being looked for; must not be null

    • getTint

    • isConcealed

      public boolean isConcealed()

    • getStatMultiplier

      public float getStatMultiplier(Stat stat)
      Returns what running effects together multiply the given effective stat by, which is 1 when nothing is running. Effects compose, so two buffs multiply rather than one winning.

    • getTint

      public com.badlogic.gdx.graphics.Color getTint()
      Returns the combined tint of running effects, or null when none tints. Tints multiply, so being hidden and buffed at once shows both.

    • addStatusEffect

      public void addStatusEffect(StatusEffect effect)
      Puts a status effect on this entity. The controller now owns its lifetime: it is ticked each frame and its StatusEffect.onRemoved() runs once when it comes off.

    • update

      public void update()
      Updates the state of all status effects. Removes status effects that return true from update, then tells each removed effect, so no callback ever sees a half-cleared list.

    • dispose

      public void dispose()
      Ends every effect on this entity and stops the controller for good.

      Each effect still running is removed and told, so none is left believing it is on an entity that no longer exists. A disposed controller ticks nothing further and refuses new effects.

      Overrides:
      dispose in class Component
